headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress create data-leak and prompt/cascade risks; slim’s privileged container tooling amplifies impact.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airbyte has broad network egress and API-based I/O, while slim reads/writes filesystem artifacts and uses interactive command execution. A shared workspace or copied outputs could let attacker-controlled content from Airbyte be treated as instructions by slim. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF Airbyte outputs are copied into slim’s stdin or files without sanitization
IF both agents operate on the same workspace directory
mitigations: Separate workspaces for each agent
Disable copy-paste of raw agent outputs into commands
Add a manual review step before slim executes generated text
Use read-only mounts for Airbyte outputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad egress; slim touches filesystem artifacts, environment variables, and certificate private keys, and also has broad egress. If they share a workspace or credentials, sensitive material can flow from one agent’s files into the other’s outbound requests. The pairwise leak path is plausible but not directly documented, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Airbyte and slim share a filesystem or mounted volume
IF slim is pointed at directories containing secrets or business data
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared directories
Mount only the minimum required paths into slim
Rotate any credentials exposed to slim
Review outbound destinations before running either agent
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent network allowlists

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte can call APIs and slim can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, read/write the filesystem, and use Docker Engine APIs. Even though slim does not modify git state and its concurrency model is isolated, both can mutate shared files or external services if pointed at the same targets. That overlapping write surface creates a real conflict path.
conditions: IF both agents target the same filesystem path or API resource
IF Airbyte writes artifacts that slim later rewrites or deletes
mitigations: Assign disjoint target directories
Run one agent at a time on shared resources
Snapshot inputs before slim mutates them
Use file locks for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add resource-level coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airbyte can produce data outputs that slim may consume while inspecting container images and filesystem artifacts. Slim’s interactive command execution means it could act on Airbyte-produced content without a built-in verification step. The pair does not prove automatic trust, but the output-to-input chain is plausible enough to warrant medium severity.
conditions: IF slim consumes Airbyte-generated files or command text
IF no human verification occurs between Airbyte output and slim action
mitigations: Insert a manual review gate
Require checksums for transferred artifacts
Use a dry-run mode before any destructive slim action
Log and compare expected vs actual outputs
requires-engineering: add schema validation for inter-agent handoffs

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte touches business data, while slim touches certificate private keys, environment variables, and registry credentials. If business data or regulated secrets are processed together, differing retention or residency expectations can be violated. The profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdiction mismatch, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated business data is routed through slim’s image-analysis session
IF registry credentials or private keys are stored alongside Airbyte outputs
mitigations: Classify data before handing it to slim
Keep regulated data out of container-analysis workspaces
Purge temporary artifacts after each run
Restrict access to credential-bearing files
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries
